title: Adirondack chair
about: Lounge chair with wide armrests and tall slatted back
blurb: The Adirondack chair is an outdoor lounge chair with wide armrests, a tall slatted back, and a seat that is higher in the front than the back. Its name references the Adirondack Mountains in Upstate New York.

title: Aeron chair
about: Office chair designed by Don Chadwick and Bill Stumpf
blurb: The Aeron chair is an office chair manufactured and sold by American furniture company Herman Miller. Introduced in 1994, it was designed by Don Chadwick and Bill Stumpf and departed from the design of traditional office chairs by eschewing upholstery in favor of fabric mesh.

title: Anglepoise lamp
blurb: A desk lamp balanced on springs so that it stays wherever you point it.

title: Antimacassar
about: Small cloth placed over the backs of furniture
blurb: An antimacassar /ˌæntɪməˈkæsər/ is a small cloth placed over the backs or arms of chairs, or the head or cushions of a sofa, to prevent soiling of the permanent fabric underneath.

title: Arc lamp
about: Lamp that produces light by an electric arc
blurb: An arc lamp or arc light is a lamp that produces light by an electric arc. The carbon arc light, which consists of an arc between carbon electrodes in air, invented by Humphry Davy in the first decade of the 1800s, was the first practical electric light.

title: Barcelona chair
about: Chair by Mies van der Rohe, Lilly Reich
blurb: The Barcelona chair is a chair designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich for the German Pavilion at the International Exposition of 1929, hosted in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

title: Bayeux Tapestry
about: Embroidery depicting the 1066 Norman invasion of England
blurb: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered cloth nearly 70 metres long and 50 centimetres tall that depicts the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England, led by William, Duke of Normandy, and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

title: Beaker
about: Glass container used in laboratories
blurb: In laboratory equipment, a beaker is generally a cylindrical container with a flat bottom. Most also have a small spout to aid pouring, as shown in the picture. Beakers are available in a wide range of sizes, from one milliliter up to several liters.

title: Bean bag chair
blurb: A sack of pellets that takes the shape of whoever falls into it.

title: Bed
about: Piece of furniture used as a place to sleep or relax
blurb: A bed is a piece of furniture that is used as a place to sleep, rest, and relax. Most modern beds consist of a soft, cushioned mattress on a bed frame. The mattress rests either on a solid base, often wood slats, or a sprung base.

title: Bedroom
about: Private room having at least one bed; used for rest or relaxation
blurb: A bedroom or bedchamber is a room situated within a residential or accommodation unit, primarily used for sleeping. A typical Western bedroom contains as bedroom furniture one or two beds, a clothes closet, and bedside table and dressing table, both of which usually contain drawers.

title: Bench
about: Type of long seat
blurb: A bench is a long seat on which several people may sit at the same time. Benches are typically made of wood, but may also be made of metal, stone, or synthetic materials. Many benches have back rests, while others do not and can be accessed from either side. Arm rests are another common feature.

title: Billiard table
about: Bounded table on which cue sports are played
blurb: A billiard table or billiards table is a bounded table on which cue sports are played. In the modern era, all billiards tables provide an elevated flat surface usually made of quarried slate, that is covered with cloth, and surrounded by vulcanized rubber cushions.

title: Blacklight
about: Light fixture that emits long-wave ultraviolet light and very little visible light
blurb: A blacklight, also called a UV-A light, Wood's lamp, or ultraviolet light, is a lamp that emits long-wave ultraviolet light and very little visible light.

title: Bookcase
about: Furniture used to store books
blurb: A bookcase also called a bookshelf, is a piece of furniture with horizontal shelves, often in a cabinet, used to store books or other printed materials. Bookcases are used in private homes, public and university libraries, offices, schools, and bookstores.

title: Brazier
about: Container used to burn charcoal or other solid fuel
blurb: A brazier is a container used to burn charcoal or other solid fuel for cooking, heating, and/or rituals. It often takes the form of a metal box or bowl with feet, but in some places it is made of terracotta, a type of clay. Its elevation helps circulate air, feeding more oxygen to the fire.

title: Bunk bed
about: Bed in which one bed frame is stacked on top of another bed
blurb: Look up bunk bed or bunkbed in Wiktionary, the free dictionary. A bunk bed or set of bunks is a type of bed in which one bed frame is stacked on top of another bed, allowing two or more sleeping-places to occupy the floor space usually required by just one.

title: Cabinetry
about: Box-shaped piece of furniture with doors
blurb: A cabinet is a case or cupboard with shelves or drawers for storing or displaying items. Some cabinets are stand-alone while others are built into a wall or are attached to it like a medicine cabinet. Cabinets are typically made of wood, coated steel, or synthetic materials.

title: Candelabra
about: Candle holder with multiple arms
blurb: A candelabrum, or candelabra, is a type of candlestick which has multiple branches to hold several candles as opposed to only one. "Candelabra" can be used to describe a variety of candle holders including chandeliers.

title: Candle
about: Wick embedded in solid flammable substance
blurb: A candle is an ignitable wick embedded in wax, or another flammable solid substance such as tallow, that provides light, and in some cases, a fragrance. A candle can also provide heat or a method of keeping time.

title: Carpet
about: Textile floor covering
blurb: A carpet or rug is a floor covering made with textile that typically consists of an upper layer of pile attached to a backing.

title: Casserole
about: Variety of cooking pot and general category of foods cooked inside it
blurb: A casserole is a kind of large, deep pan or bowl used for cooking a variety of dishes in the oven; it is also a category of foods cooked in such a vessel. To distinguish the two uses, the pan can be called a "casserole dish" or "casserole pan", whereas the food is simply "a casserole".

title: Cauldron
about: Large kettle
blurb: A cauldron is a large pot or kettle used for cooking or boiling, typically over an open fire. It often features a lid, an arc-shaped hanger, and/or integral handles or feet.

title: Chair
about: Piece of furniture for sitting on
blurb: A chair is a type of seat, typically designed for one person and consisting of one or more legs, a flat or slightly angled seat, and a back rest. It may be made of wood, metal, or synthetic materials, and may be padded or upholstered in various colors and fabrics. Chairs vary in design.

title: Chaise longue
about: Upholstered chair
blurb: A chaise longue is an upholstered sofa in the shape of a chair that is long enough to support the legs of the sitter. For the unupholstered outdoor furniture see sunlounger. In modern French, the term chaise longue refers to any long sitting chair, such as a deckchair.

title: Chandelier
blurb: A branched light fixture hung from the ceiling, often dripping with cut glass.

title: Chemex Coffeemaker
about: Pour-over style glass coffeemaker
blurb: The Chemex Coffeemaker is a manual pour-over style glass coffeemaker, invented by Peter Schlumbohm in 1941, manufactured by the Chemex Corporation in Chicopee, Massachusetts.

title: Chip pan
about: Steep cooking pan used for deep-frying
blurb: A chip pan is a deep-sided cooking pan used for deep-frying. Chip pans are named for their traditional use in frying chips. Today, they are made from either aluminium or stainless steel, although in the past were commonly made from cast iron.

title: Chopsticks
about: Shaped pairs of sticks used as kitchen and eating utensils
blurb: Chopsticks are shaped pairs of equal-length sticks that have been used as kitchen and eating utensils in most countries of the Sinosphere for over three millennia. They are held in the dominant hand, secured by fingers, and wielded as extensions of the hand, to pick up food.

title: Christmas lights
about: Decorative lighting used at Christmastime
blurb: Christmas lights are lights often used for decoration in celebration of Christmas, often on display throughout the Christmas season including Advent and Christmastide. The custom goes back to when Christmas trees were decorated with candles, which symbolized Christ being the light of the world.

title: Clothes dryer
about: Appliance used for drying wet clothes
blurb: A clothes dryer is a powered household appliance that is used to remove moisture from a load of clothing, bedding and other textiles, usually after they are washed in the washing machine.

title: Coffee filter
about: Coffee brewing utensil
blurb: A coffee filter is a filter used for various coffee brewing methods including but not limited to drip coffee filtering. Filters made of paper, cloth, or plastic, metal or porcelain are used.

title: Coffeemaker
about: Cooking appliance used to brew coffee
blurb: A coffeemaker, coffee maker or coffee machine is a cooking appliance used to brew coffee. While there are many different types of coffeemakers, the two most common brewing principles use gravity or pressure to move hot water through coffee grounds.

title: Color rendering index
about: Accuracy of light source in showing color of objects
blurb: A color rendering index is a quantitative measure of the ability of a light source to reveal the colors of various objects faithfully in comparison with a natural or standard light source.

title: Color temperature
about: Property of light sources related to black-body radiation
blurb: Color temperature is a parameter describing the color of a visible light source by comparing it to the color of light emitted by an idealized opaque, non-reflective body, known as a black body.

title: Commode
about: Type of furniture (or toilet)
blurb: Commode is a term that may refer to multiple different pieces of furniture. The Oxford English Dictionary has multiple meanings of "commode".

title: Compressor
about: Machine to increase pressure of gas by reducing its volume
blurb: A compressor is a mechanical device that increases the pressure of a gas by reducing its volume. An air compressor is a specific type of gas compressor. Many compressors can be staged, that is, the gas is compressed several times in steps or stages, to increase discharge pressure.

title: Cookware and bakeware
about: Food preparation containers
blurb: Cookware and bakeware is food preparation equipment, such as cooking pots, frying pans, baking sheets etc. used in kitchens. Cookware is used on a stove or range cooktop, while bakeware is used in an oven. Some utensils are considered both cookware and bakeware.

title: Coronation Chair
about: Wooden chair used in British coronations
blurb: The Coronation Chair, also known as St Edward's Chair or King Edward's Chair, is an ancient wooden chair that is used by British monarchs when they are invested with regalia and crowned at their coronation.

title: Couch
about: Furniture for seating multiple people
blurb: A couch, also known as a sofa, settee, chesterfield, or davenport, is a cushioned piece of furniture that can seat multiple people. It is commonly found in the form of a bench with upholstered armrests and is often fitted with springs and tailored cushion and pillows.

title: Credenza
about: Dining room sideboard cupboard
blurb: A credenza is a dining room sideboard or display cabinet, usually made of burnished and polished wood and decorated with marquetry. The top would often be made of marble, or another decorative liquid- and heat-resistant stone. The credenza started as a rough table with a cloth draped over it.

title: Cubicle
about: Office furniture meant to allow for concentration
blurb: A cubicle is an enclosed office that is separated from neighboring workspaces, with partitions that are usually 5–6 feet tall. Its purpose is to isolate office workers and managers from the sights and noises of an open workspace so that they may concentrate with fewer distractions.

title: Cup
about: Small container for drinks
blurb: A cup is a small container used to hold liquids for drinking, typically with a flattened hemispherical shape and an open "mouth", and often with a capacity of about 6–16 US fluid ounces. Cups may be made of pottery, glass, metal, wood, stone, polystyrene, plastic, lacquerware, or other materials.

title: Cupboard
about: Furniture enclosing items stored in a home
blurb: A cupboard is a piece of furniture for enclosing dishware or grocery items that are stored in a home. The term is sometimes also used for any form of cabinet or enclosed bookcase.

title: Curule seat
about: Foldable and transportable chair
blurb: A curule seat is a design of a foldable and transportable chair noted for its uses in Ancient Rome and Europe through to the 20th century.

title: Cutlery
about: Eating utensils
blurb: Cutlery are utensils used for serving and eating food at the dining table — originally referring to just knives, whereas forks and spoons were silverware — all part of flatware or tableware, these both encompassing crockery as well.

title: Desk
about: Type of table often used in a school or office setting
blurb: A desk or bureau is a piece of furniture with a flat table-style work surface used in a school, office, home or the like for academic, professional or domestic activities such as reading, writing, or using equipment such as a computer.

title: Dishwasher
about: Machine that washes dishes automatically
blurb: A dishwasher is a machine that is used to clean dishware, cookware, and cutlery automatically. Unlike manual dishwashing, which relies on physical scrubbing to remove soiling, the mechanical dishwasher cleans by spraying hot water, typically between 45 and 75 °C, at the dishes, with lower…

title: Display case
about: Cabinet with transparent surfaces
blurb: A display case is a cabinet with one or often more transparent tempered glass surfaces, used to display objects for viewing. A display case may appear in an exhibition, museum, retail store, restaurant, or house.

title: Divan
about: Couch-like sitting furniture
blurb: A divan is a piece of couch-like sitting furniture or, in some regions, a box-spring-based bed. Primarily found in West Asia, a divan is a long seat formed of a mattress laid against the side of the room, upon the floor, or a raised structure or frame, with cushions to lean against.

title: Dutch oven
about: Cooking pot with thick walls and a lid
blurb: A Dutch oven, Dutch pot, or casserole dish is a thick-walled cooking pot with a tight-fitting lid. Dutch ovens are usually made of seasoned cast iron; however, some Dutch ovens are instead made of cast aluminium, or ceramic.

title: Duvet
about: Type of bedding
blurb: A duvet, usually called a comforter or quilt in American English, and a doona in Australian English, is a type of bedding consisting of a soft flat bag filled with down, feathers, wool, cotton, silk, or a synthetic alternative, and is typically protected with a removable cover, similar to a pillow…

title: Eames Lounge Chair
blurb: A moulded plywood and leather armchair from 1956, designed to feel like a well-used baseball mitt.

title: Eating utensil etiquette
about: Social conventions of cutlery usage
blurb: Various customary etiquette practices exist regarding the placement and use of eating utensils in social settings. These practices vary from culture to culture. Fork etiquette, for example, differs in Europe, the United States, and Southeast Asia, and continues to change.

title: Ejection seat
about: Emergency aircraft escape system
blurb: In aircraft, an ejection seat or ejector seat is a system designed to rescue the pilot or other crew of an aircraft in an emergency. In most designs, the seat is propelled out of the aircraft by an explosive charge or rocket motor, carrying the pilot with it.

title: Electric light
about: Device for producing light from electricity
blurb: An electric light, lamp, or light bulb is an electrical device that produces light from electricity. It is the most common form of artificial lighting. Lamps usually have a base made of ceramic, metal, glass, or plastic that secures them in the socket of a light fixture.

title: Espresso machine
about: Device used to brew espresso coffee
blurb: An espresso machine is a device that brews coffee by rapidly forcing heated, pressurized water through a small, compressed cake of finely ground coffee and a coffee filter to produce a thick, concentrated coffee called espresso. Espresso machines vary significantly in design and operation.

title: Fan
about: Machine used to produce air flow
blurb: A fan is a powered machine that creates airflow. A fan consists of rotating vanes or blades, generally made of wood, plastic, or metal, which act on the air. The rotating assembly of blades and hub is known as an impeller, rotor, or runner.

title: Filing cabinet
about: Piece of office furniture
blurb: A filing cabinet is a piece of office furniture for storing paper documents in file folders. In the most simple context, it is an enclosure for drawers in which articles are stored. The two most common forms of filing cabinets are vertical files and lateral files.

title: Flare
about: Pyrotechnic light source
blurb: A flare is a type of pyrotechnic that produces a bright light or intense heat without an explosion. Flares are used for distress signaling, illumination, or defensive countermeasures in civilian and military applications.

title: Flashlight
about: Portable hand-held electric light
blurb: A flashlight or electric torch, usually shortened to torch, is a portable hand-held electric lamp. Formerly, the light source typically was a miniature incandescent light bulb, but these have been displaced by light-emitting diodes since the early 2000s.

title: Fluorescent lamp
about: Lamp using fluorescence to produce light
blurb: A fluorescent lamp, or fluorescent tube, is a low-pressure mercury-vapor gas-discharge lamp that uses fluorescence to produce visible light. An electric current in the gas excites mercury vapor, to produce ultraviolet and make a phosphor coating in the lamp glow.

title: Fork
about: Eating utensil
blurb: In cutlery or kitchenware, a fork is a utensil, now usually made of metal, whose long handle terminates in a head that branches into several narrow and often slightly curved tines with which one can spear foods either to hold them to cut with a knife or to lift them to the mouth.

title: Four-poster bed
about: Bed with a vertical column at each corner
blurb: A four-poster bed or tester bed is a bed with four vertical columns, one in each corner, that support a tester, or upper panel or bedknobs. This tester or panel will often have rails to allow curtains to be pulled around the bed.

title: French press
about: Coffee brewing device
blurb: A French press, also known as a cafetière, cafetière à piston, caffettiera a stantuffo, press pot, coffee press or coffee plunger is a coffee brewing device, although it can also be used for other tasks.

title: Frying pan
about: Flat bottomed pan for cooking food on a stove
blurb: A frying pan, also called frypan or skillet, is a flat-bottomed cookware used for frying, searing and browning foods. It typically ranges from 20 to 30 cm in diameter with relatively low sides that flare outwards, a long handle and no lid.

title: Furniture
about: Objects used to support human activities
blurb: Furniture refers to objects intended to support various human activities, such as seating, eating, storing items, working, and sleeping. Furniture is also used to hold objects at a convenient height for work, or to store things.

title: Futon
about: Traditional Japanese bedding
blurb: A futon is a traditional Japanese style of bedding. A complete futon set consists of a mattress and a duvet. Both elements of a futon bedding set are pliable enough to be folded and stored away in a large closet during the day.

title: Globe
blurb: A spherical model of the Earth on a tilted axis, made to be spun and stopped with a finger.

title: Glow stick
about: Self-contained, short-term light source
blurb: A glow stick, also known as a light stick, chem light, light wand, light rod, and rave light, is a self-contained, short-term light source. It consists of a translucent plastic tube containing isolated substances that, when combined, produce light through chemiluminescence.

title: Halogen lamp
about: Incandescent lamp variety
blurb: A halogen lamp is an incandescent lamp consisting of a tungsten filament sealed in a compact transparent envelope that is filled with a mixture of an inert gas and a small amount of a halogen, such as iodine or bromine.

title: Hammock
blurb: A sling of cloth or netting hung between two points, for sleeping, swinging and doing nothing.

title: Home appliance
about: Machine for household uses
blurb: A home appliance, also referred to as a domestic appliance, an electric appliance or a household appliance, is a machine which assists in household functions such as cooking, cleaning and food preservation.

title: Hoosier cabinet
about: Type of cupboard serving as a workstation
blurb: A Hoosier cabinet or Hoosier is a type of cupboard or free-standing kitchen cabinet that also serves as a workstation. It was popular in the first few decades of the 20th century in the United States, since most houses did not have built-in kitchen cabinetry.

title: Hospital bed
about: Bed designed for hospital patients
blurb: A hospital bed or hospital cot is a bed specially designed for hospitalized patients and others requiring health care. These beds have special features both for the comfort and well-being of the patient and for the convenience of health care workers.

title: Hudson's Bay point blanket
about: Wool blanket traded by Hudson's Bay Company
blurb: Hudson's Bay point blankets are woollen blankets originally made for the Hudson's Bay Company in British North America, now Canada and the United States.

title: Induction cooking
about: Direct induction heating of cooking vessels
blurb: Induction cooking is a cooking process using direct electrical induction heating of cookware, rather than relying on flames or heating elements. Induction cooking allows high power and very rapid increases in temperature to be achieved: changes in heat settings are instantaneous.

title: Instant Pot
about: Canadian brand of multicookers (2010–)
blurb: Instant Pot is a brand of automated multicookers manufactured by Instant Pot Brands. It is sometimes colloquially referred to as InstaPot. The multicookers are electronically-controlled combined pressure cookers and slow cookers.

title: Kettle
about: Vessel used to boil water
blurb: A kettle, sometimes called a tea kettle or teakettle, is a device specialized for boiling water, commonly with a lid, spout, and handle.

title: Kitchen cabinet
about: Kitchen furniture
blurb: Kitchen cabinets are the built-in furniture installed in many kitchens for storage of food, cooking equipment, and often silverware and dishes for table service. Appliances such as refrigerators, dishwashers, and ovens are often integrated into kitchen cabinetry.

title: Kitchen utensil
about: Tool used for food preparation
blurb: A kitchen utensil is a small hand-held tool used for food preparation. Common kitchen tasks include cutting food items to size, heating food on an open fire or on a stove, baking, grinding, mixing, blending, and measuring; different utensils are made for each task.

title: Kotatsu
about: Low, wooden table used in Japan, often with a heat source underneath
blurb: A kotatsu is a low, wooden table frame covered by a futon, or heavy blanket, upon which a table top sits. Underneath is a heat source, formerly a charcoal brazier but now electric, often built into the table itself.

title: Lantern
about: Portable lighting device
blurb: Look up lantern in Wiktionary, the free dictionary. A lantern is a source of lighting, often portable.

title: Lava lamp
blurb: Blobs of coloured wax rising and sinking through liquid in a glowing glass vessel, since 1963.

title: LED lamp
about: Electric light that produces light using LEDs
blurb: An LED lamp or LED light is an electric light that produces light using light-emitting diodes. LED lamps are significantly more energy-efficient than equivalent incandescent lamps and fluorescent lamps.

title: Light fixture
about: Electrical device with an electric lamp
blurb: A light fixture, light fitting or luminaire is an electrical lighting device containing one or more light sources, such as light bulbs, and all the accessory components required for its operation to provide illumination to the environment.

title: Lighting
about: Deliberate use of light to achieve practical or aesthetic effects
blurb: Lighting or illumination is the deliberate use of light to achieve practical or aesthetic effects. Lighting includes the use of both artificial light sources like lamps and light fixtures, as well as natural illumination by capturing daylight.

title: Microwave oven
about: Kitchen cooking appliance
blurb: A microwave oven, or simply microwave, is an electric oven that heats and cooks food by exposing it to electromagnetic radiation in the microwave frequency range. This induces polar molecules in the food to rotate and produce thermal energy in a process known as dielectric heating.

title: Mirror
about: Object that reflects an image
blurb: A mirror, also known as a looking glass, is an object that reflects an image. Light that bounces off a mirror forms an image of whatever is in front of it, which is then focused through the lens of the eye or a camera. Mirrors reverse the direction of light at an angle equal to its incidence.

title: Mirror test
about: Animal self-awareness test
blurb: The mirror test—sometimes called the mark test, mirror self-recognition test, red spot technique, or rouge test—is a behavioral technique developed in 1970 by American psychologist Gordon Gallup Jr. to determine whether an animal possesses the ability of visual self-recognition.

title: Mixer
about: Kitchen device
blurb: A mixer is a kitchen device that uses a gear-driven mechanism to rotate a set of "beaters" in a bowl containing the food or liquids to be prepared by mixing them. Mixers help automate the repetitive tasks of stirring, whisking or beating.

title: Moka pot
blurb: The eight-sided aluminium stovetop coffee maker found in nearly every Italian kitchen.

title: Monobloc
about: Stackable polypropylene chair
blurb: The Monobloc chair is a lightweight stackable polypropylene chair, usually white in color, often described as the world's most common plastic chair. The name comes from mono- and bloc, in this case referring to an object injection moulded in a single piece.

title: Mug
about: Type of cup
blurb: A mug is a type of cup, a drinking vessel usually intended for hot drinks such as coffee, hot chocolate, or tea. Mugs have handles and usually hold a larger amount of fluid than other types of cups such as teacups or coffee cups. Typically, a mug holds approximately 250–350 ml of liquid.

title: Music box
blurb: A box that plays a tune when a pinned cylinder plucks the teeth of a steel comb.

title: Office chair
about: Chair designed for use at an office
blurb: An office chair, or desk chair, is a type of chair that is designed for use at a desk in an office. It is usually a swivel chair, with a set of wheels for mobility and adjustable height.

title: Ottoman
about: Furniture
blurb: An ottoman is a piece of furniture. Generally, ottomans have neither backs nor arms. They may be an upholstered low couch or a smaller cushioned seat used as a table, stool or footstool.

title: Oven
about: Enclosed chamber for heating objects
blurb: An oven is a tool that is used to expose materials to a hot environment. Ovens contain a hollow chamber and provide a means of heating the chamber in a controlled way. In use since antiquity, they have been used to accomplish a wide variety of tasks requiring controlled heating.

title: Penny lick
about: Small glass for serving ice cream
blurb: A penny lick was a small 80 oz glass for serving ice cream, used in London, England, and elsewhere in the late nineteenth century and early twentieth century. Street vendors would sell the contents of the glass for one penny.

title: Pillow
about: Cushion for the head
blurb: A pillow is a soft fabric cushion used to support the head or body. Pillows are a form of bedding that supports the head and neck. Some pillows are purely decorative. In contemporary western culture, pillows are encased in a plain or patterned fabric envelope.

title: Plane mirror
about: Mirror with a flat reflecting surface
blurb: A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat reflective surface. For light rays striking a plane mirror, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. The angle of the incidence is the angle between the incident ray and the surface normal.

title: Pressure cooker
about: Device for preparing food
blurb: A pressure cooker is a sealed vessel used for cooking food with the use of high pressure steam and water or a water-based liquid, in a process called pressure cooking.

title: Pyrex
about: Brand of glassware
blurb: Pyrex is a type of borosilicate glass developed by Corning Incorporated in 1908. Pyrex was first introduced to the public in 1915, as a brand of clear, low-thermal-expansion glassware products, whose resistance to chemicals, electricity, and heat made it ideal for laboratory glassware and…

title: Pythagorean cup
about: Cup with a central siphon drain
blurb: A Pythagorean cup is a practical joke device in the form of a drinking cup. When it is filled beyond a certain point, a siphoning effect causes the cup to drain its entire contents through the base. The cup has been used to make statements about greed.

title: Ramekin
about: Small bowl used for culinary purposes
blurb: Look up ramekin in Wiktionary, the free dictionary. A ramekin is a small dish used for culinary purposes.

title: Refrigerator
about: Appliance for cold food storage
blurb: A refrigerator, commonly shortened to fridge, is a device designed to maintain a cold internal temperature by expelling heat.

title: Rice cooker
about: Kitchen appliance
blurb: A rice cooker or rice steamer is an automated kitchen appliance designed to boil or steam rice. It consists of a heat source, a cooking bowl, and a thermostat. The thermostat measures the temperature of the cooking bowl and controls the heat.

title: Rocking chair
blurb: A chair on two curved runners, best placed on a porch.

title: Round Table
about: Table in the Arthurian legend
blurb: The Round Table is King Arthur's famed table in the Arthurian legend, around which he and his knights congregate.

title: Samovar
about: Metal container used to heat and boil water
blurb: A samovar is a metal container traditionally used to heat and boil water. Although originating in Russia, the samovar is well known outside of the country and has spread through Russian culture to other parts of Eastern Europe, as well as West and Central and South Asia.

title: Sewing machine
about: Machine used to stitch fabric
blurb: A sewing machine is a machine used to sew fabric and materials together with thread. Sewing machines were invented during the first Industrial Revolution to decrease the amount of manual sewing work performed in clothing companies.

title: Shaker furniture
about: Furniture developed by the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing
blurb: Shaker furniture is a distinctive style of furniture developed by the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing, commonly known as Shakers, a religious sect that had guiding principles of simplicity, utility and honesty.

title: Shelf
about: Flat horizontal plane used for storage
blurb: A shelf is a flat, horizontal or sloping plane used for items that are displayed or stored in a home, business, store, or elsewhere.

title: Sky lantern
about: Small hot air balloon made to be released into the air
blurb: A sky lantern, also known as a Kongming lantern, is a small hot air balloon made of paper, with an opening at the bottom where a small fire is suspended. Sky lanterns have been made for centuries in cultures around the world, to be launched for play or as part of long-established festivities.

title: Slow cooker
about: Countertop electrical cooking appliance used to simmer food
blurb: A slow cooker is a countertop electrical cooking appliance used to simmer at a lower temperature than other cooking methods, such as baking, boiling, and frying.

title: Snow globe
blurb: A glass sphere holding a tiny scene and a flurry of snow that falls when you shake it.

title: Spoon
about: Eating utensil
blurb: A spoon is a utensil consisting of a shallow bowl, oval or round, at the end of a handle. A type of cutlery, especially as part of a place setting, it is used primarily for transferring food to the mouth.

title: Stove
about: Device used to generate heat or to cook
blurb: A stove or range is an appliance or construction that generates heat inside or atop the device using an energy source. They differ from ovens, since ovens keep their heat in closed chambers, while stoves typically allow their heat to flow outwards.

title: Street light
about: Raised source of light beside a road or path
blurb: A street light, light pole, lamp pole, lamppost, streetlamp, light standard, or lamp standard is a raised source of light on the edge of a road or path. Similar lights may be found on a railway platform.

title: Table
about: Piece of furniture with a flat top
blurb: A table is a piece of furniture with a raised flat top and is supported most commonly by 1 to 4 legs. It is used as a surface for working, eating or placing things.

title: Tablespoon
about: Kind of spoon and unit of volume
blurb: A tablespoon is a large spoon and a cooking measure of volume. In many English-speaking regions, the term now refers to a large spoon used for serving. In some regions, it is the largest type of spoon used for eating. Several systems of units of measurement define a tablespoon.

title: Tableware
about: Items used for setting a table and serving food
blurb: Tableware items are the dishware and utensils used for setting a table, serving food, and dining. The term includes cutlery, glassware, serving dishes, serving utensils, and other items used for practical as well as decorative purposes.

title: Tandoor
about: Cylindrical clay oven used in South Asian cooking
blurb: A tandoor is a large vase-shaped oven, usually made of clay. Since antiquity, tandoors have been used to bake unleavened flatbreads, such as roti and traditional lavash, as well as leavened ones, such as naan and tandoor bread or matnakash. It is also used to roast meat and vegetables.

title: Tapestry
about: Form of textile art, traditionally woven on a vertical loom
blurb: Tapestry is a form of textile art which was traditionally woven by hand on a loom. Normally it is used to create images rather than patterns.

title: Teapot
blurb: A lidded vessel with a spout and a handle, for steeping tea and settling arguments.

title: Teaspoon
about: Kind of spoon
blurb: A teaspoon is a small spoon that can be used to stir a cup of tea or coffee, or as a tool for measuring volume. The size of teaspoons ranges from about 2.5 to 7.3 mL.

title: Terrarium
blurb: A sealed glass container holding a miniature garden that waters itself.

title: The Unicorn Tapestries
about: Tapestry series from the early 16th century
blurb: The Unicorn Tapestries or the Hunt of the Unicorn is a series of seven tapestries made in the Southern Netherlands around 1495–1505, and now in The Cloisters in New York City. They were possibly designed in Paris and woven in Brussels.

title: Thermomix
about: Kitchen appliance by Vorwerk
blurb: The Thermomix is a multi-purpose kitchen appliance of the Multicooker type made by Vorwerk. The current Thermomix has a heating element, a motor for fast or slow blending and stirring, and a weighing scale.

title: Tiffany lamp
about: Type of lamp with colorful glass shade
blurb: A Tiffany lamp is a type of lamp with a glass shade designed by Louis Comfort Tiffany and collaborators, including Clara Driscoll, made in his design studio in Corona, Queens, New York City.

title: Toaster
about: Domestic appliance used for toasting foods, especially bread
blurb: A toaster is a small electric appliance that uses radiant heat to cook sliced bread into toast. When cooked the bread browns due to the maillard reaction.

title: Torch
about: Stick with a flaming end used as a source of light
blurb: A torch is a stick with combustible material at one end which can be used as a light source or to set something on fire. Torches have been used throughout history and are still used in processions, symbolic and religious events, and in juggling and entertainment.

title: Trojan Room coffee pot
about: Predecessor of the webcam
blurb: The Trojan Room coffee pot was a coffee machine located in the Computer Laboratory of the University of Cambridge, England. It was the subject of the world's first webcam, created by Quentin Stafford-Fraser and Paul Jardetzky in 1991.

title: Upholstery
about: Covering of furniture with padding, springs, webbing, and fabric or leather
blurb: Upholstery is the work of providing furniture, especially seats, with padding, springs, webbing, and fabric or leather covers. The word also refers to the materials used to upholster something.

title: Vacuum cleaner
about: Device that sucks up dirt from a surface
blurb: A vacuum cleaner, also known simply as a vacuum, is a device that uses suction, and often agitation, in order to remove dirt and other debris from carpets, hard floors, and other surfaces. The dirt is collected into a dust bag or a plastic bin.

title: Washing machine
about: Machine that washes clothes
blurb: A washing machine is a machine designed to launder clothing. The term is mostly applied to machines that use water. Other ways of doing laundry include dry cleaning and ultrasonic cleaning. Modern-day home appliances use electric power to automatically clean clothes.

title: Wassily chair
about: Chair designed by Marcel Breuer
blurb: The Wassily chair, also known as the Model B3 chair, was designed by Marcel Breuer in 1925–1926 while he was the head of the cabinet-making workshop at the Bauhaus, in Dessau, Germany.

title: Waterbed
about: Mattress filled with water
blurb: A waterbed, water mattress, or flotation mattress is a bed or mattress filled with water. Waterbeds intended for medical therapies appear in various reports through the 19th century.

title: Windsor chair
about: Type of chair with a solid wood seat and turned legs
blurb: A Windsor chair is a chair built with a solid wooden seat into which the chair-back and legs are round-tenoned, or pushed into drilled holes, in contrast to other styles of chairs whose back legs and back uprights are continuous.

title: Wok
about: Cooking vessel originating in China
blurb: A wok is a deep round-bottomed cooking pan of either indigenous Chinese origin or derived from the South Asian karahi. It is common in Greater China, and similar pans are found in parts of East, South and Southeast Asia, as well as being popular in other parts of the world.
